Tuchow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tuchów, Poland

Demolished. NOTE: the source page's address, coordinates, and city fields for this record were found to be duplicated from an unrelated cemetery entry (Żabno), so those specific fields are not used here; the coordinates above are an approximate town-center location for Tuchów itself, not the precise cemetery site. The narrative below, however, is Tuchów-specific and appears reliable. Per ESJF field researchers who interviewed a resident living adjacent to the site (house no. 73): the cemetery was largely stripped of matzevot by Nazi forces during WWII for road construction. After the war the land was registered as state property before being sold into private ownership; the private owner subsequently used an excavator to destroy remaining traces of the cemetery. The same resident recalled seeing human bones exposed during that excavation work, though their ultimate fate is unknown; she believed some tombstone remains may still exist somewhere on the grounds. The cemetery also contained a WWI military burial section. The current landowners do not permit access to the property.
